title: Compiler Construction
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Compiler Construction curriculum (lexical/syntax/semantic analysis, parsing, symbol tables, code generation and optimization), directly matching LASU's own CSC319 'Compiler Construction' course description (compilers/assemblers/interpreters review, lexical/expression analysis, grammars, top-down/bottom-up parsing, LR grammars and analysers, symbol tables, run-time storage organization, code generation/optimization).

questions.question: What is the primary function of a compiler?
options: To translate source code written in a high-level language into another language, typically machine or object code
To execute source code line by line without translation
To manage a computer's file system
To design the graphical user interface of an application
questions.correct_answer: To translate source code written in a high-level language into another language, typically machine or object code
questions.explanation: A compiler translates an entire program from a source language (e.g., C) into a target language (e.g., machine code) before execution.

questions.question: How does an interpreter differ from a compiler?
options: An interpreter executes source code statements directly, one at a time, without producing a separate standalone object file
An interpreter always produces faster-running programs than a compiler
A compiler cannot detect syntax errors
An interpreter and a compiler are functionally identical
questions.correct_answer: An interpreter executes source code statements directly, one at a time, without producing a separate standalone object file
questions.explanation: Unlike a compiler, which translates the whole program before execution, an interpreter reads and executes source code statements directly, typically without generating a persistent machine-code file.

questions.question: What distinguishes an assembler from a compiler?
options: An assembler translates assembly language (a low-level, largely one-to-one mnemonic representation) into machine code, while a compiler translates high-level languages
An assembler can only translate Java programs
A compiler works only with binary input
There is no meaningful difference between them
questions.correct_answer: An assembler translates assembly language (a low-level, largely one-to-one mnemonic representation) into machine code, while a compiler translates high-level languages
questions.explanation: Assemblers convert low-level assembly mnemonics into machine code on a largely one-to-one basis, whereas compilers perform a more complex many-to-one translation from high-level source code.

questions.question: What is the first phase of a typical compiler?
options: Lexical analysis
Code generation
Semantic analysis
Optimization
questions.correct_answer: Lexical analysis
questions.explanation: Lexical analysis (scanning) is the first phase, where the compiler reads the source code character by character and groups them into tokens.

questions.question: What is a 'token' in the context of lexical analysis?
options: A categorized sequence of characters representing a meaningful unit, such as a keyword, identifier, or operator
A single bit of machine code
The final compiled executable file
A syntax error message
questions.correct_answer: A categorized sequence of characters representing a meaningful unit, such as a keyword, identifier, or operator
questions.explanation: Tokens are the smallest meaningful units identified by the lexical analyzer, such as keywords, identifiers, literals, operators, and punctuation.

questions.question: What formal tool is most commonly used to specify the patterns that define tokens during lexical analysis?
options: Regular expressions
Context-free grammars
Turing machines
Relational algebra
questions.correct_answer: Regular expressions
questions.explanation: Regular expressions are used to define the lexical patterns (e.g., identifier or number formats) that a lexical analyzer recognizes and converts into tokens.

questions.question: What type of automaton is commonly used to implement a lexical analyzer that recognizes tokens?
options: A Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA)
A Turing machine
A pushdown automaton exclusively
A linear bounded automaton
questions.correct_answer: A Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA)
questions.explanation: Regular expressions describing token patterns are typically converted into a DFA (via an NFA), which efficiently recognizes tokens by processing input characters one at a time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of syntax analysis (parsing) in a compiler?
options: To check whether the sequence of tokens conforms to the grammatical rules of the language and build a parse tree
To allocate memory for variables at runtime
To translate the program into machine code directly
To manage input/output operations
questions.correct_answer: To check whether the sequence of tokens conforms to the grammatical rules of the language and build a parse tree
questions.explanation: The parser takes the stream of tokens from lexical analysis and verifies it against the language's grammar, producing a parse tree (or syntax tree) representing its structure.

questions.question: What formalism is typically used to define the syntax (grammar) of a programming language?
options: Context-free grammar (often expressed in BNF)
Regular expressions only
Finite state machines only
Relational calculus
questions.correct_answer: Context-free grammar (often expressed in BNF)
questions.explanation: Programming language syntax is typically specified using context-free grammars, often written in Backus-Naur Form (BNF) or a similar notation.

questions.question: What is the key difference between top-down and bottom-up parsing?
options: Top-down parsing builds the parse tree from the root downward, while bottom-up parsing builds it from the leaves upward
Top-down parsing cannot handle recursive grammar rules
Bottom-up parsing does not use a grammar
There is no difference between the two
questions.correct_answer: Top-down parsing builds the parse tree from the root downward, while bottom-up parsing builds it from the leaves upward
questions.explanation: Top-down parsers (e.g., recursive descent, LL) start from the start symbol and derive the input, while bottom-up parsers (e.g., LR) start from the input tokens and reduce toward the start symbol.

questions.question: What does an LL(1) parser represent?
options: A top-down parser that scans input Left to right, produces a Leftmost derivation, using 1 token of lookahead
A bottom-up parser using 1 symbol of lookahead
A parser that only works on regular languages
A parser generator for lexical analysis only
questions.correct_answer: A top-down parser that scans input Left to right, produces a Leftmost derivation, using 1 token of lookahead
questions.explanation: LL(1) denotes a top-down parsing method: Left-to-right scan, Leftmost derivation, with 1 token of lookahead used to decide which production to apply.

questions.question: What does an LR parser represent, and how does it differ fundamentally from LL parsing?
options: LR is a bottom-up parsing technique that scans Left to right and produces a Rightmost derivation in reverse
LR is a top-down parsing technique identical to LL
LR only works for regular expressions, not grammars
LR requires no stack during parsing
questions.correct_answer: LR is a bottom-up parsing technique that scans Left to right and produces a Rightmost derivation in reverse
questions.explanation: LR parsers are bottom-up: they scan input left to right and construct a rightmost derivation in reverse, generally handling a broader class of grammars than LL parsers.

questions.question: What data structure is central to shift-reduce parsing (used in LR parsers)?
options: A stack
A queue
A hash table
A binary search tree
questions.correct_answer: A stack
questions.explanation: Shift-reduce parsers use a stack to hold grammar symbols and states, shifting input tokens onto the stack and reducing sequences according to grammar productions.

questions.question: What is a 'symbol table' used for in a compiler?
options: To store information about identifiers, such as their type, scope, and memory location, for use throughout compilation
To store the final generated machine code
To hold error messages produced by the lexer
To represent the target CPU's instruction set
questions.correct_answer: To store information about identifiers, such as their type, scope, and memory location, for use throughout compilation
questions.explanation: The symbol table is a central data structure that records attributes of identifiers (variables, functions, etc.), accessed and updated across multiple compilation phases.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of semantic analysis in a compiler?
options: To check for meaning-related errors, such as type mismatches, that syntax analysis alone cannot detect
To generate the final machine code
To read source code characters and form tokens
To optimize the register allocation of the target machine
questions.correct_answer: To check for meaning-related errors, such as type mismatches, that syntax analysis alone cannot detect
questions.explanation: Semantic analysis verifies context-sensitive correctness, such as type checking, scope resolution, and ensuring variables are declared before use, which a purely syntactic check cannot catch.

questions.question: What is 'type checking' during semantic analysis?
options: Verifying that operations are performed on operands of compatible types according to the language's type rules
Counting the number of tokens in a program
Allocating physical memory addresses to variables
Formatting source code for readability
questions.correct_answer: Verifying that operations are performed on operands of compatible types according to the language's type rules
questions.explanation: Type checking ensures expressions and statements use operands whose types are compatible with the operations being performed, catching errors like adding a string to an integer where disallowed.

questions.question: What is an 'intermediate representation' (or intermediate code) in compiler design?
options: A machine-independent representation of the source program used as a bridge between the front end and back end of the compiler
The final executable binary file
The original, unmodified source code
A list of syntax errors found during parsing
questions.correct_answer: A machine-independent representation of the source program used as a bridge between the front end and back end of the compiler
questions.explanation: Intermediate code (e.g., three-address code) abstracts away source and target language details, simplifying optimization and enabling retargeting to different machine architectures.

questions.question: What is the purpose of code optimization in a compiler?
options: To improve the generated code's efficiency (speed or size) without changing its observable behavior
To introduce additional syntax errors for testing
To translate the program into a different high-level language
To remove all comments from the source file
questions.correct_answer: To improve the generated code's efficiency (speed or size) without changing its observable behavior
questions.explanation: Code optimization transforms the intermediate or target code to run faster or use less memory while preserving the program's original semantics.

questions.question: What is 'dead code elimination' as a compiler optimization technique?
options: Removing code that can never be executed or whose results are never used
Adding extra instructions to slow down execution intentionally
Renaming all variables to shorter names
Converting the program into assembly language
questions.correct_answer: Removing code that can never be executed or whose results are never used
questions.explanation: Dead code elimination identifies and removes statements that have no effect on the program's observable output, reducing code size and improving performance.

questions.question: What is the final phase of a typical compiler pipeline?
options: Code generation
Lexical analysis
Parsing
Semantic analysis
questions.correct_answer: Code generation
questions.explanation: Code generation is the final phase, where the optimized intermediate representation is translated into target machine code or assembly.

questions.question: What is 'register allocation' in the code generation phase?
options: The process of assigning a program's variables to a limited number of CPU registers to minimize memory access
The process of allocating disk space for the compiled executable
Creating new entries in the symbol table
Assigning line numbers to source code statements
questions.correct_answer: The process of assigning a program's variables to a limited number of CPU registers to minimize memory access
questions.explanation: Since CPU registers are limited and much faster than main memory, register allocation strategically assigns frequently used variables to registers to improve performance.

questions.question: What is 'run-time storage organization' concerned with in compiler design?
options: How memory is organized and managed for a program during its execution, including the stack, heap, and static/global areas
How source code files are organized on disk before compilation
The layout of tokens produced by the lexer
The formatting of compiler error messages
questions.correct_answer: How memory is organized and managed for a program during its execution, including the stack, heap, and static/global areas
questions.explanation: Run-time storage organization defines how a compiled program's memory is laid out during execution, covering the stack (for function calls/local variables), heap (dynamic allocation), and static storage.

questions.question: What is an 'activation record' (or stack frame) used for in run-time storage organization?
options: To store information needed for a single execution of a procedure/function, such as local variables, parameters, and the return address
To store the entire compiled program's machine code
To hold the source code's comments
To represent the symbol table permanently
questions.correct_answer: To store information needed for a single execution of a procedure/function, such as local variables, parameters, and the return address
questions.explanation: An activation record is pushed onto the call stack for each function invocation, holding local variables, parameters, saved registers, and the return address.

questions.question: In compiler theory, what is a 'grammar' used to define?
options: The syntactic structure and valid sentences (programs) of a language
The meaning of variable names chosen by a programmer
The physical hardware architecture of the target machine
The color scheme of an IDE
questions.correct_answer: The syntactic structure and valid sentences (programs) of a language
questions.explanation: A formal grammar specifies the set of rules (productions) that generate all syntactically valid strings (programs) in a language.

questions.question: What is meant by a grammar being 'ambiguous'?
options: There exists at least one string that can be generated by more than one distinct parse tree
The grammar has no production rules at all
The grammar can generate an infinite language
The grammar uses only terminal symbols
questions.correct_answer: There exists at least one string that can be generated by more than one distinct parse tree
questions.explanation: Ambiguity occurs when a single string in the language can be derived through multiple different parse trees, which complicates unambiguous interpretation during parsing.

questions.question: What is the role of a 'recognizer' in the context of formal languages and compiler front ends?
options: A program or automaton that determines whether a given input string belongs to a specified language
A tool for generating random test data
A device for formatting source code output
A component that only handles runtime errors
questions.correct_answer: A program or automaton that determines whether a given input string belongs to a specified language
questions.explanation: A recognizer accepts or rejects an input string based on whether it conforms to the rules of a formal language, forming the theoretical basis for lexical analyzers and parsers.

questions.question: Why is FORTRAN historically significant as a reference language when teaching or studying early compiler construction?
options: It was one of the first widely used high-level languages, and its compiler was a landmark early example of automatic translation to machine code
It was designed exclusively for web development
It has no formal grammar
It cannot be compiled, only interpreted
questions.correct_answer: It was one of the first widely used high-level languages, and its compiler was a landmark early example of automatic translation to machine code
questions.explanation: FORTRAN, developed in the 1950s, was among the first high-level programming languages, and building its compiler pioneered many foundational compiler construction techniques still studied today.

questions.question: What is a 'translator writing system' in compiler construction?
options: A tool or set of tools used to help automatically generate compilers or parts of compilers from formal language specifications
A word processor used by programmers
A hardware device for translating binary to decimal
A system for translating natural language documentation
questions.correct_answer: A tool or set of tools used to help automatically generate compilers or parts of compilers from formal language specifications
questions.explanation: Translator (or compiler) writing systems, such as parser generators, automate portions of compiler construction based on formal grammar and lexical specifications.

questions.question: What is the purpose of constructing an LR parsing table during bottom-up parser construction?
options: To guide the parser's shift/reduce decisions based on the current state and input symbol
To store the final compiled machine code instructions
To list all lexical errors found in the source
To record variable memory addresses only
questions.correct_answer: To guide the parser's shift/reduce decisions based on the current state and input symbol
questions.explanation: The LR parsing table encodes, for each combination of parser state and lookahead symbol, whether to shift, reduce, accept, or report an error, driving the parsing process.
